dedupe_keys.name: egg supply chain network model for germany fskx model object bfr

description: This model estimates how chicken eggs move from farms through packing and processing to consumers across Germany's districts, so that the spread of a contaminated batch or a disruption in supply can be traced. The producers are Petra Ganas, Marcel Fuhrmann and Matthias Filter of the German Federal Institute for Risk Assessment, who published it in the Food Modelling Journal in 2021. It is a supply chain network model: the user chooses a type of actor in the chain as input, and the model returns estimated egg flows between NUTS-3 districts as a table together with a choropleth map of quantities. Coverage is Germany at district level. The model, its data and annotations are packaged as a single file following the Food Safety Knowledge Exchange (FSKX) standard, available as a free download from Zenodo under a CC0 public domain dedication, and it can run in the desktop FSK-Lab software or online. Caveats: flows are modelled from aggregate statistics, not observed shipments, it covers one commodity, and it needs the FSK tools to open. Simulation uses: tracing food safety incidents, estimating which regions depend on which producers, and testing supply disruption scenarios in food network models. Related records: the food shock trade model (model-global-food-shock-trade) works at international scale.
